title: Connectors
description: 135 questions: the original 120 plus 15 Moderate–Hard items. Select Moderate–Hard for close alternatives and complete meaning checks. The label is a reviewed training target, not an independently calibrated exam rating.

packs.title: Find the cause and the result

questions.prompt: The bank tightened verification ___ several fraudulent applications had been detected.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Detected fraud is the reason for tighter checks.
explanation.rule: Because introduces a reason clause with a subject and verb.
explanation.model: The bank tightened verification because several fraudulent applications had been detected.

rejects.reason: Requires a noun phrase or -ing form, not this finite clause.
Would present fraud as a concession, not the reason.
A result adverb cannot replace the reason conjunction here.
Introduces a condition that does not preserve this factual reason.

questions.prompt: Several fraudulent applications were detected; ___, the bank tightened verification.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The first clause states the cause; the second states its consequence.
explanation.rule: Therefore links a result clause; the semicolon and comma provide the structure.
explanation.model: Several fraudulent applications were detected; therefore, the bank tightened verification.

rejects.reason: Suggests an outcome despite the first fact, rather than because of it.
States an alternative consequence if an action is not taken.
Would require a reason clause, not this result-adverb position.
Marks contrast rather than the stated consequence.

questions.prompt: The workshop postponed production ___ a shortage of essential materials.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The shortage causes the postponement.
explanation.rule: Because of takes a noun phrase: a shortage of materials.
explanation.model: The workshop postponed production because of a shortage of essential materials.

rejects.reason: Needs a subject and finite verb after it.
Introduces a purpose clause, not a noun phrase giving a cause.
Needs a clause and introduces concession.
Would say production was postponed in spite of the shortage, changing the intended reason.

questions.prompt: The auditor found an anomaly, ___ she examined the supporting invoices.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The anomaly prompted further examination.
explanation.rule: So coordinates a consequence clause after a comma.
explanation.model: The auditor found an anomaly, so she examined the supporting invoices.

rejects.reason: Cannot introduce the finite clause she examined.
A standalone linking adverb would need stronger punctuation here; the comma alone makes a splice.
Turns the examination into a condition rather than a response.
Contrasts two facts rather than showing this response.

questions.prompt: The instructions were ambiguous; ___, applicants interpreted them differently.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Different interpretations follow from unclear instructions.
explanation.rule: Consequently introduces the result, not a contrast.
explanation.model: The instructions were ambiguous; consequently, applicants interpreted them differently.

rejects.reason: Would reverse a relationship, which is not intended.
A subordinate conjunction does not fit this semicolon-adverb-comma construction.
Introduces an alternative conditional result.
Signals concession rather than the expected effect.

questions.prompt: ___ the proposal was commercially viable, the board rejected it because its legal risks were unresolved.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Viability would favour approval, yet rejection occurred.
explanation.rule: Although introduces a factual concession followed by a clause.
explanation.model: Although the proposal was commercially viable, the board rejected it because its legal risks were unresolved.

rejects.reason: Cannot directly introduce the finite clause the proposal was.
A result adverb cannot introduce this subordinate clause.
Makes viability a hypothetical condition.
Makes viability the reason for rejection.

questions.prompt: ___ its commercial viability, the proposal was rejected because its legal risks were unresolved.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The noun phrase names a favourable fact that did not prevent rejection.
explanation.rule: Despite takes a noun phrase; although takes a clause.
explanation.model: Despite its commercial viability, the proposal was rejected because its legal risks were unresolved.

rejects.reason: Requires a purpose/result clause, not this noun phrase.
Cannot directly take its commercial viability as its complete subordinate clause.
Makes viability the cause of rejection.
Requires a condition clause.

questions.prompt: The first plan protects liquidity, ___ the second ties up most available cash.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Two plans have contrasting effects on ready cash.
explanation.rule: Whereas contrasts two clauses; it does not state a cause.
explanation.model: The first plan protects liquidity, whereas the second ties up most available cash.

rejects.reason: Introduces a condition, not a comparison of actual plans.
Cannot directly introduce this finite clause.
Would make the second plan a consequence of the first.
Would make the second plan the reason for the first.

questions.prompt: The system is faster; ___, incomplete records can still delay approval.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The second fact limits the apparent benefit of speed.
explanation.rule: However is a linking adverb; the semicolon and comma separate the clauses correctly.
explanation.model: The system is faster; however, incomplete records can still delay approval.

rejects.reason: Claims that incomplete records delaying approval is the result of greater speed.
Also imposes an unsupported result relationship.
Does not fit this linking-adverb construction.
Indicates similarity rather than a limitation.

questions.prompt: The firm remained profitable ___ a sharp rise in operating costs.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Higher costs threaten profit, but profitability remained.
explanation.rule: In spite of takes the noun phrase a sharp rise.
explanation.model: The firm remained profitable in spite of a sharp rise in operating costs.

rejects.reason: Needs a finite concession clause.
Introduces intended purpose, not this noun phrase.
Needs a finite reason clause.
Makes rising costs the reason for profitability.

questions.prompt: Your application cannot be processed ___ you submit the required identity documents.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Without submission, processing is impossible.
explanation.rule: Unless means except if; this sentence states that submission is necessary.
explanation.model: Your application cannot be processed unless you submit the required identity documents.

rejects.reason: Cannot introduce the finite clause you submit.
Cannot directly introduce the finite clause you submit.
Treats submission as an actual concessive fact.
Introduces contrast, not a necessary condition.

questions.prompt: The repayment arrangement will remain available ___ the borrower continues to meet the agreed conditions.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Continued access depends on continued compliance.
explanation.rule: Provided that introduces a required condition.
explanation.model: The repayment arrangement will remain available provided that the borrower continues to meet the agreed conditions.

rejects.reason: Contrasts facts instead of making access conditional.
Requires a noun phrase, not this clause.
Introduces replacement or preference, not eligibility.
Makes compliance a concession rather than a condition.

questions.prompt: A verification check is compulsory: the payment will proceed ___ the account details have been confirmed.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Confirmation is necessary; the sentence does not promise that confirmation alone guarantees payment.
explanation.rule: Only if states a necessary condition.
explanation.model: A verification check is compulsory: the payment will proceed only if the account details have been confirmed.

rejects.reason: Expresses a wish rather than a necessary condition.
Allows payment without confirmed details.
Says confirmation is the exception preventing payment, reversing the rule.
Treats confirmation as a concession.

questions.prompt: Keep a copy of the receipt ___ the original is misplaced later.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The copy is kept now as preparation for a possible later loss.
explanation.rule: In case introduces a precaution; it does not mean waiting until the problem happens.
explanation.model: Keep a copy of the receipt in case the original is misplaced later.

rejects.reason: Does not express preparation for a risk.
Makes keeping a copy depend on the original not being misplaced.
Cannot introduce this finite clause.
Delays keeping a copy until the original has already been lost.

questions.prompt: The safety inspection is mandatory, ___ the factory has had no recent accidents.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Inspection remains necessary regardless of whether the reassuring circumstance holds.
explanation.rule: Even if marks a condition that will not change the main requirement.
explanation.model: The safety inspection is mandatory, even if the factory has had no recent accidents.

rejects.reason: Cannot take this clause directly.
Treats the past accident record as the purpose of inspection.
Creates an exemption when no accidents have occurred.
Makes absence of accidents a necessary condition for inspection.

questions.prompt: The officer checked the documents ___ releasing the payment; verification came first.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Verification precedes release.
explanation.rule: Before can take an -ing form: before releasing.
explanation.model: The officer checked the documents before releasing the payment; verification came first.

rejects.reason: Reverses the stated order.
Cannot directly take this -ing phrase as a full concession clause here.
Does not link this verb phrase to a time relation.
Cannot directly take releasing as a complete finite reason clause.

questions.prompt: Please remain in the waiting area ___ your token number is called.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Waiting continues up to the calling of the number.
explanation.rule: Until marks an endpoint for an ongoing state or action.
explanation.model: Please remain in the waiting area until your token number is called.

rejects.reason: Makes waiting depend on the number already being called, reversing the intended instruction.
Suggests a factual concession, not the endpoint.
Expresses contrast rather than duration.
Requires a noun phrase.

questions.prompt: The team sent an update ___ the review was completed; there was no intervening delay.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The update immediately follows completion.
explanation.rule: As soon as states immediate succession.
explanation.model: The team sent an update as soon as the review was completed; there was no intervening delay.

rejects.reason: Cannot introduce this finite clause.
Turns a completed event into a hypothetical condition.
Makes completion an exception preventing the update.
Reverses the order.

questions.prompt: The clerk verified the figures ___ the supervisor checked the supporting records; both tasks happened at the same time.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Both tasks are simultaneous.
explanation.rule: While introduces an overlapping action; here the explicit cue selects its time sense.
explanation.model: The clerk verified the figures while the supervisor checked the supporting records; both tasks happened at the same time.

rejects.reason: Places one task after the other.
Cannot introduce this subordinate time clause.
Places one task before the other.
States a condition, not simultaneous work.

questions.prompt: ___ the documents arrive tomorrow, the officer will examine them.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The ordinary future-time clause uses the present simple arrive.
explanation.rule: When + present simple can refer to a future event before will in the main clause.
explanation.model: When the documents arrive tomorrow, the officer will examine them.

rejects.reason: Does not form the required subordinate time clause.
Cannot introduce the finite clause.
Makes the examination conditional on the documents not arriving, reversing the intended sequence.
Requires a noun phrase.

questions.prompt: The notice was rewritten ___ customers could understand the charges before applying.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Understanding the charges is the intended benefit of rewriting.
explanation.rule: So that introduces a purpose clause with its own subject and verb.
explanation.model: The notice was rewritten so that customers could understand the charges before applying.

rejects.reason: Would make understanding an exception to rewriting.
Cannot take the finite clause customers could understand.
Introduces a contrast rather than a purpose.
Would state a concession rather than the intended purpose.

questions.prompt: The officer called the applicant ___ clarify the discrepancy.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The call is made with the aim of clarifying.
explanation.rule: In order to is followed by the base verb clarify.
explanation.model: The officer called the applicant in order to clarify the discrepancy.

rejects.reason: Would need a condition clause.
Would need a noun or -ing form.
Would need a subject and finite verb after it.
Would need a complete reason clause.

questions.prompt: The instructions were ___ clear that no applicant asked for clarification.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The that-clause describes the consequence of a high degree of clarity.
explanation.rule: So + adjective + that is the degree-result pattern.
explanation.model: The instructions were so clear that no applicant asked for clarification.

rejects.reason: Such normally modifies a noun phrase, not clear alone.
Does not modify the adjective in this construction.
Does not form the so ... that pair.
Does not form a degree-result construction.

questions.prompt: It was ___ a detailed explanation that even new employees understood the process.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: A noun phrase, a detailed explanation, follows the blank.
explanation.rule: Such + a/an + adjective + noun + that expresses degree and result.
explanation.model: It was such a detailed explanation that even new employees understood the process.

rejects.reason: So cannot directly precede this a + adjective + noun sequence.
Does not modify this noun phrase to form the result construction.
Cannot create the required degree-result pair.
Introduces concession, not this noun-phrase pattern.

questions.prompt: The programme improves access ___ preserves essential verification checks; both benefits are intended.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The two benefits are added, not opposed.
explanation.rule: And coordinates the parallel verbs improves and preserves.
explanation.model: The programme improves access and preserves essential verification checks; both benefits are intended.

rejects.reason: Cannot directly coordinate the two finite verbs.
A linking adverb cannot coordinate these verbs in this position.
Makes preserving checks an exception rather than an additional benefit.
Introduces a contrast not stated in the prompt.

questions.prompt: The application was rejected ___ the required signature was missing.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: A complete subject-verb clause gives the reason.
explanation.rule: Because + clause; because of + noun phrase.
explanation.model: The application was rejected because the required signature was missing.

rejects.reason: Makes the missing signature a result of rejection.
Cannot directly take the finite clause the signature was missing.
Introduces an exception rather than the stated factual reason.
Cannot take the finite clause and would reverse the expected relation.

questions.prompt: ___ the missing signature, the application was rejected.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The missing signature is a noun phrase expressing the cause.
explanation.rule: Because of + noun phrase.
explanation.model: Because of the missing signature, the application was rejected.

rejects.reason: Needs a finite concession clause.
Turns the missing signature into something rejection occurred in spite of.
Requires a purpose/result clause.
Needs a finite clause here.

questions.prompt: The applicant remained calm ___ receiving an unexpected rejection.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: Remaining calm contrasts with the distress the rejection might cause.
explanation.rule: Despite can take an -ing phrase: despite receiving.
explanation.model: The applicant remained calm despite receiving an unexpected rejection.

rejects.reason: Does not form a condition clause with receiving here.
Cannot directly take receiving here as a full clause.
Cannot directly take receiving as the reason clause.
Does not form this prepositional concession structure.

questions.prompt: ___ the applicant received an unexpected rejection, she remained calm.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: A factual adverse event did not prevent calmness.
explanation.rule: Although + subject + finite verb.
explanation.model: Although the applicant received an unexpected rejection, she remained calm.

rejects.reason: Also requires a noun phrase rather than a finite clause.
Is a result adverb, not a concession conjunction.
Cannot directly take the applicant received.
Makes the actual rejection a hypothetical exception.

questions.prompt: The officer checked ___ the account number was correct or not.
questions.instructions: Choose the connector that fits both the relationship and the sentence structure.

explanation.clue: The check concerns two possibilities: correct or not correct.
explanation.rule: Whether introduces alternatives; whether ... or not is a standard pattern.
explanation.model: The officer checked whether the account number was correct or not.

rejects.reason: States an exception, not an indirect choice question.
Cannot introduce the finite question clause.
Requires a noun phrase, not an embedded question.
Cannot introduce an indirect question.

questions.prompt: The regulator found repeated reporting failures. Those failures caused it to impose stringent checks.
questions.instructions: Choose the one grammatical sentence preserving all supplied facts and their stated relationship.
options: Because it imposed stringent checks, the regulator found repeated reporting failures.
Although it found repeated reporting failures, the regulator imposed stringent checks.
Because it found repeated reporting failures, the regulator imposed stringent checks.
Unless it found repeated reporting failures, the regulator imposed stringent checks.
Because of it found repeated reporting failures, the regulator imposed stringent checks.
questions.answer: Because it found repeated reporting failures, the regulator imposed stringent checks.

explanation.clue: Reporting failures cause the checks, not the reverse.
explanation.rule: Keep the reason in the because-clause and the response in the main clause.
explanation.model: Because it found repeated reporting failures, the regulator imposed stringent checks.

rejects.option: Because it imposed stringent checks, the regulator found repeated reporting failures.
rejects.reason: Reverses the explicit causal relationship.

rejects.option: Although it found repeated reporting failures, the regulator imposed stringent checks.
rejects.reason: Substitutes concession for the stated cause.

rejects.option: Unless it found repeated reporting failures, the regulator imposed stringent checks.
rejects.reason: Turns actual facts into an exception condition.

rejects.option: Because of it found repeated reporting failures, the regulator imposed stringent checks.
rejects.reason: Because of cannot take this finite clause.

questions.prompt: The instructions were ambiguous. That ambiguity caused applicants to make inconsistent submissions.
questions.instructions: Choose the one grammatical sentence preserving all supplied facts and their stated relationship.
options: The instructions were ambiguous, so applicants made inconsistent submissions.
The instructions were ambiguous unless applicants made inconsistent submissions.
Applicants made inconsistent submissions, so the instructions were ambiguous.
The instructions were ambiguous, however applicants made inconsistent submissions.
Despite applicants making inconsistent submissions, the instructions were ambiguous.
questions.answer: The instructions were ambiguous, so applicants made inconsistent submissions.

explanation.clue: Inconsistency follows from ambiguous instructions.
explanation.rule: So joins a stated cause to its result.
explanation.model: The instructions were ambiguous, so applicants made inconsistent submissions.

rejects.option: The instructions were ambiguous unless applicants made inconsistent submissions.
rejects.reason: Creates an exception instead of preserving the actual causal facts.

rejects.option: Applicants made inconsistent submissions, so the instructions were ambiguous.
rejects.reason: Reverses cause and effect.

rejects.option: The instructions were ambiguous, however applicants made inconsistent submissions.
rejects.reason: Comma + however does not correctly join two independent clauses, and the link should be causal.

rejects.option: Despite applicants making inconsistent submissions, the instructions were ambiguous.
rejects.reason: Replaces the causal relation with concession.

questions.prompt: The firm lacked liquidity. This shortage, not weak long-term assets, forced it to delay payment.
questions.instructions: Choose the one grammatical sentence preserving all supplied facts and their stated relationship.
options: The firm lacked liquidity because it delayed payment, not because its long-term assets were weak.
The firm delayed payment because its long-term assets were weak, not because it lacked liquidity.
The firm delayed payment because it lacked liquidity, not because its long-term assets were weak.
The firm delayed payment unless it lacked liquidity and its long-term assets were weak.
Although the firm lacked liquidity, it delayed payment because its long-term assets were weak.
questions.answer: The firm delayed payment because it lacked liquidity, not because its long-term assets were weak.

explanation.clue: The original explicitly separates the actual cause from the rejected cause.
explanation.rule: Preserve both the cause and the not-because qualification.
explanation.model: The firm delayed payment because it lacked liquidity, not because its long-term assets were weak.

rejects.option: The firm lacked liquidity because it delayed payment, not because its long-term assets were weak.
rejects.reason: Reverses the actual cause.

rejects.option: The firm delayed payment because its long-term assets were weak, not because it lacked liquidity.
rejects.reason: Exchanges the accepted and rejected causes.

rejects.option: The firm delayed payment unless it lacked liquidity and its long-term assets were weak.
rejects.reason: Changes facts into a condition and introduces the wrong asset claim.

rejects.option: Although the firm lacked liquidity, it delayed payment because its long-term assets were weak.
rejects.reason: Adds a cause that the original rejects.

questions.prompt: The evidence corroborated the complaint. For that reason, the bank reopened the case.
questions.instructions: Choose the one grammatical sentence preserving all supplied facts and their stated relationship.
options: Since the bank reopened the case, the evidence corroborated the complaint.
The bank reopened the case so that the evidence had corroborated the complaint.
Despite the evidence corroborated the complaint, the bank reopened the case.
Since the evidence corroborated the complaint, the bank reopened the case.
Even if the evidence corroborated the complaint, the bank reopened the case.
questions.answer: Since the evidence corroborated the complaint, the bank reopened the case.

explanation.clue: Evidence supports the complaint, leading to reopening.
explanation.rule: Since can introduce a reason; this context supplies the causal reading.
explanation.model: Since the evidence corroborated the complaint, the bank reopened the case.

rejects.option: Since the bank reopened the case, the evidence corroborated the complaint.
rejects.reason: Makes reopening the reason for corroboration.

rejects.option: The bank reopened the case so that the evidence had corroborated the complaint.
rejects.reason: A later action cannot have the stated past evidence as its intended purpose.

rejects.option: Despite the evidence corroborated the complaint, the bank reopened the case.
rejects.reason: Despite cannot directly take a finite clause.

rejects.option: Even if the evidence corroborated the complaint, the bank reopened the case.
rejects.reason: Changes established evidence into a hypothetical concession.

questions.prompt: The insurer received incomplete records. The incompleteness was the reason it withheld approval.
questions.instructions: Choose the one grammatical sentence preserving all supplied facts and their stated relationship.
options: Despite the incompleteness of the records, the insurer withheld approval.
Owing to the incompleteness of the records, the insurer withheld approval.
The insurer received incomplete records because it withheld approval.
Owing to the insurer received incomplete records, it withheld approval.
The insurer withheld approval in order to receive incomplete records.
questions.answer: Owing to the incompleteness of the records, the insurer withheld approval.

explanation.clue: Incomplete records cause approval to be withheld.
explanation.rule: Owing to is followed by a noun phrase.
explanation.model: Owing to the incompleteness of the records, the insurer withheld approval.

rejects.option: Despite the incompleteness of the records, the insurer withheld approval.
rejects.reason: Makes withholding concessive rather than caused by incompleteness.

rejects.option: The insurer received incomplete records because it withheld approval.
rejects.reason: Reverses the cause.

rejects.option: Owing to the insurer received incomplete records, it withheld approval.
rejects.reason: Owing to cannot directly take this finite clause.

rejects.option: The insurer withheld approval in order to receive incomplete records.
rejects.reason: Turns the cause into an implausible intended purpose.

packs.title: Join facts without losing the concession

questions.prompt: The bank introduced stringent checks. Nevertheless, fraudulent applications continued to arrive.
questions.instructions: Choose the one grammatical sentence preserving all supplied facts and their stated relationship.
options: Although the bank introduced stringent checks, fraudulent applications continued to arrive.
Because the bank introduced stringent checks, fraudulent applications continued to arrive.
The bank introduced stringent checks so that fraudulent applications would continue to arrive.
Despite the bank introduced stringent checks, fraudulent applications continued to arrive.
Unless the bank introduced stringent checks, fraudulent applications continued to arrive.
questions.answer: Although the bank introduced stringent checks, fraudulent applications continued to arrive.

explanation.clue: The checks did not prevent the continuing problem.
explanation.rule: Although takes a finite clause; preserve the nevertheless relationship.
explanation.model: Although the bank introduced stringent checks, fraudulent applications continued to arrive.

rejects.option: Because the bank introduced stringent checks, fraudulent applications continued to arrive.
rejects.reason: Claims the checks caused the fraudulent applications.

rejects.option: The bank introduced stringent checks so that fraudulent applications would continue to arrive.
rejects.reason: Changes prevention into a purpose of encouraging fraud.

rejects.option: Despite the bank introduced stringent checks, fraudulent applications continued to arrive.
rejects.reason: Despite cannot directly take a finite clause.

rejects.option: Unless the bank introduced stringent checks, fraudulent applications continued to arrive.
rejects.reason: Changes factual concession into an exception condition.

questions.prompt: The proposal was viable. Even so, it was rejected because the evidence for demand was tenuous.
questions.instructions: Choose the one grammatical sentence preserving all supplied facts and their stated relationship.
options: Despite the proposal was viable, it was rejected because the evidence for demand was tenuous.
Although the proposal was viable, but it was rejected because the evidence for demand was tenuous.
Despite being viable, the proposal was rejected because the evidence for demand was tenuous.
Unless the proposal was viable, it was rejected because the evidence for demand was tenuous.
Because it was viable, the proposal was rejected despite strong evidence for demand.
questions.answer: Despite being viable, the proposal was rejected because the evidence for demand was tenuous.

explanation.clue: Viability is conceded; weak demand evidence remains the rejection reason.
explanation.rule: Despite can take being viable; because retains the actual cause.
explanation.model: Despite being viable, the proposal was rejected because the evidence for demand was tenuous.

rejects.option: Despite the proposal was viable, it was rejected because the evidence for demand was tenuous.
rejects.reason: Despite cannot directly take the finite clause.

rejects.option: Although the proposal was viable, but it was rejected because the evidence for demand was tenuous.
rejects.reason: In standard exam English, although and but should not both connect the same pair of clauses.

rejects.option: Unless the proposal was viable, it was rejected because the evidence for demand was tenuous.
rejects.reason: Changes an established favourable fact into an exception condition.

rejects.option: Because it was viable, the proposal was rejected despite strong evidence for demand.
rejects.reason: Changes both the rejection reason and the quality of evidence.

questions.prompt: Digital access improved. However, rural participation remained limited.
questions.instructions: Choose the one grammatical sentence preserving all supplied facts and their stated relationship.
options: Digital access improved unless rural participation remained limited.
Digital access improved because rural participation remained limited.
Digital access improved; however, rural participation remained limited.
Digital access improved, however rural participation remained limited.
Digital access improved, so rural participation remained limited.
questions.answer: Digital access improved; however, rural participation remained limited.

explanation.clue: An improvement is qualified by an unresolved limitation.
explanation.rule: However needs appropriate separation between independent clauses.
explanation.model: Digital access improved; however, rural participation remained limited.

rejects.option: Digital access improved unless rural participation remained limited.
rejects.reason: Changes factual contrast into a condition.

rejects.option: Digital access improved because rural participation remained limited.
rejects.reason: Turns the remaining limitation into the cause of improvement.

rejects.option: Digital access improved, however rural participation remained limited.
rejects.reason: A comma alone does not correctly join these independent clauses using however.

rejects.option: Digital access improved, so rural participation remained limited.
rejects.reason: Changes the qualification into an asserted consequence.

questions.prompt: The first scheme alleviated immediate hardship. In contrast, the second exacerbated repayment pressure.
questions.instructions: Choose the one grammatical sentence preserving all supplied facts and their stated relationship.
options: The first scheme alleviated immediate hardship so that the second could exacerbate repayment pressure.
Because the first scheme alleviated immediate hardship, the second exacerbated repayment pressure.
The first scheme alleviated immediate hardship, whereas the second exacerbated repayment pressure.
The first scheme exacerbated repayment pressure, whereas the second alleviated immediate hardship.
Despite the first scheme alleviated immediate hardship, the second exacerbated repayment pressure.
questions.answer: The first scheme alleviated immediate hardship, whereas the second exacerbated repayment pressure.

explanation.clue: The original compares opposite effects of two different schemes.
explanation.rule: Whereas can contrast two factual clauses.
explanation.model: The first scheme alleviated immediate hardship, whereas the second exacerbated repayment pressure.

rejects.option: The first scheme alleviated immediate hardship so that the second could exacerbate repayment pressure.
rejects.reason: Turns the second scheme’s harm into the first scheme’s purpose.

rejects.option: Because the first scheme alleviated immediate hardship, the second exacerbated repayment pressure.
rejects.reason: Introduces a causal link not stated.

rejects.option: The first scheme exacerbated repayment pressure, whereas the second alleviated immediate hardship.
rejects.reason: Swaps the effects assigned to each scheme.

rejects.option: Despite the first scheme alleviated immediate hardship, the second exacerbated repayment pressure.
rejects.reason: Despite cannot directly introduce the finite clause.

questions.prompt: The officer was cognizant of the discrepancy. In spite of that awareness, he approved the transfer.
questions.instructions: Choose the one grammatical sentence preserving all supplied facts and their stated relationship.
options: Even though the officer was cognizant of the discrepancy, he approved the transfer.
The officer was not cognizant of the discrepancy, so he approved the transfer.
Because the officer was cognizant of the discrepancy, he approved the transfer.
Despite the officer was cognizant of the discrepancy, he approved the transfer.
Even if the officer were cognizant of the discrepancy, he would approve the transfer.
questions.answer: Even though the officer was cognizant of the discrepancy, he approved the transfer.

explanation.clue: Awareness is a fact that did not prevent approval.
explanation.rule: Even though introduces a factual concession; even if would change it into a hypothetical.
explanation.model: Even though the officer was cognizant of the discrepancy, he approved the transfer.

rejects.option: The officer was not cognizant of the discrepancy, so he approved the transfer.
rejects.reason: Reverses the stated fact of awareness.

rejects.option: Because the officer was cognizant of the discrepancy, he approved the transfer.
rejects.reason: Claims awareness was the reason for approval rather than a conceded obstacle.

rejects.option: Despite the officer was cognizant of the discrepancy, he approved the transfer.
rejects.reason: Despite cannot directly take this finite clause.

reference.meaning: A possible circumstance does not alter the main conclusion.
reference.trap: Keep hypothetical status distinct from factual even though.

reference.meaning: Prepares for a possible later circumstance.
reference.pattern: take precaution in case possible event
reference.trap: In case is not the same as taking action only after the event occurs.
reference.hinglish: pehle se taiyari, agar baad mein zarurat pade

reference.meaning: Places one event earlier or later than another.
reference.trap: Preserve which event happens first.

reference.meaning: Marks the endpoint of a continuing action or restriction.
reference.trap: Do not replace a time endpoint with a different condition without checking meaning.

reference.meaning: One event follows immediately after another.
reference.trap: Ordinary future time clauses use present forms, not automatic will.

reference.meaning: Formal immediate succession.
reference.pattern: No sooner had + subject + past participle + than clause
reference.trap: Check inversion, than and the original event order.

reference.meaning: Formal near-immediate succession.
reference.pattern: Hardly/Scarcely had + subject + past participle + when clause
reference.trap: In this paired pattern check inversion and do not substitute than.

reference.meaning: The main outcome happens no earlier than the specified circumstance.
reference.pattern: Only after/when clause + auxiliary + main subject + verb
reference.trap: Invert the main clause, not the subordinate time clause.
reference.hinglish: sirf iske baad; main clause invert

reference.meaning: Restricts an action until a specified point.
reference.pattern: Not until time/clause + inverted main clause
reference.trap: After did use the base verb.
reference.hinglish: tab tak nahi; fronted form mein inversion

reference.meaning: Often introduces the intended outcome; it can also express result in suitable contexts.
reference.pattern: action so that + subject + modal/finite verb
reference.trap: Do not force in order to before a complete subject-verb clause.
reference.hinglish: taaki: next clause ka subject ho sakta hai

reference.meaning: Introduces an intended action.
reference.trap: For a different subject use an appropriate for + subject + to structure, not a bare finite clause.

reference.meaning: Connects a degree of quality with its result.
reference.trap: Distinguish from such + noun phrase.

reference.meaning: Connects an emphasised noun phrase with its result.
reference.pattern: such + a/an + adjective + noun + that clause
reference.trap: Do not use such directly as a substitute for so before an adjective alone.

reference.meaning: Adds another fact or benefit.
reference.pattern: and coordinates; moreover links separated clauses
reference.trap: Do not invent a causal link between two facts merely being added.

reference.meaning: Adds and emphasises two parallel points.
reference.pattern: Not only did + subject + base verb, but ... also ...
reference.trap: Fronted not only requires inversion; maintain parallel structures.
reference.hinglish: dono points; pehle clause mein inversion

reference.meaning: Chooses or substitutes one alternative instead of another.
reference.trap: As well as would add Y instead of excluding it.

reference.meaning: Introduces alternatives or an indirect yes/no question.
reference.pattern: whether X or Y; whether or not
reference.trap: Do not change an either-way obligation into an only-if requirement.

reference.meaning: Excludes a stated subset or circumstance.
reference.trap: An exception to a group is not the same as a full unless-clause.

reference.meaning: Expresses an equal degree of a quality.
reference.trap: More normally pairs with than, not as.

reference.meaning: Introduces the content of a statement, belief or acknowledgement.
reference.trap: Sometimes a blank is reported content, not cause or positive/negative tone.
